_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); semiconductor signals with NVIDIA's rule-T thresholds; the listing rule (NVDA listed 1999-01-22)

pit_profile.why: 'NVIDIA pioneered accelerated computing to help solve the most challenging computational problems.' 'The market for our products is intensely competitive and is characterized by rapid technological change and evolving industry standards.' Its current competitors include 'suppliers and licensors designing discrete and integrated GPUs, custom chips and other accelerated computing solutions, such as Advanced Micro Devices, or AMD, and Intel Corporation, or Intel' and 'large internet services companies with internal teams designing chips that incorporate accelerated computing functionality as part of their internal solutions or platforms, such as Alibaba Group, Alphabet, and Amazon' (FY2022 10-K); CYCLICAL kept although the 10-K no longer calls the business cyclical (the BKR FY2015 rule; the class label only); the 10-K names AI as the field NVIDIA builds platforms for, a market it serves rather than a substitute for its products, so no theme in taxonomy_eras.json applies (the FY2013 10-K's cloud reading), and chips designed in-house by large cloud and internet companies, like GPUs integrated into other processors, stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

classification.quality_note: 'NVIDIA pioneered accelerated computing to help solve the most challenging computational problems.' Its current competitors include 'suppliers and licensors designing discrete and integrated GPUs, custom chips and other accelerated computing solutions, such as Advanced Micro Devices, or AMD, and Intel Corporation, or Intel' and 'large internet services companies with internal teams designing chips that incorporate accelerated computing functionality as part of their internal solutions or platforms, such as Alibaba Group, Alphabet, and Amazon' (FY2022 10-K); CYCLICAL kept although the 10-K no longer calls the business cyclical (the BKR FY2015 rule; the class label only); the 10-K names AI as the field NVIDIA builds platforms for, a market it serves rather than a substitute for its products, so no theme in taxonomy_eras.json applies (the FY2013 10-K's cloud reading), and chips designed in-house by large cloud and internet companies, like GPUs integrated into other processors, stay here (the PEP obesity rule). cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 1.75x; +191% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.48; conservative 2yr +4%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -31.8%/yr (worst year FY13-FY22, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +42.9%/yr (Q1 FY23 guide YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +42.9%/yr (FY13-FY22 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +111.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY13-FY22, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NVDA (retrospective, 2022-04-14) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 1.75x (87.2% downside to Bear $27.21 / +49.7% upside to Bull $318.33) | Adj composite 2.75 vs market 2.27: gap +0.48 [MODESTLY UNDERVALUED] | +191% above the EPP floor $73.15 (19x FY23E $3.85) | Conservative 2-yr case: +4.4% total (+2.2%/yr) | At 55.2x FY23E the 15% hurdle price $281.14 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +52.8% YoY in Q4 FY22, forward revenues +40.2-45.9% (Q1 FY23 revenue guide (Q4 FY22 release)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
